1.note: Here and throughout the chapter, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

2.q: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them that a man or a woman]

The phrase **and say to them** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.

Here and in 6:3–21, the masculine language refers generically to men or women, as the phrase “A man or a woman” earlier in this verse shows. See the chapter introduction for more information. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [when he or she does something wonderful]

The implication is that when someone makes a vow to become a Nazirite, they are making a serious and special commitment to Yahweh. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [when he makes a special vow, the vow of]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to vow to be]

The phrase **to make separate to Yahweh** is a common expression of this culture that means “to dedicate oneself to Yahweh” or “to set oneself apart for service to Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to set himself apart for Yahweh]

3.note: The phrase **make separate from** is a common expression of his culture to mean “completely avoid” or “abstain from.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he shall completely avoid]

The term **intoxicating drink** refers to any alcoholic beverage made from grains or other substances. If your readers would not be familiar with what intoxicating drink is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and any drink with alcohol in it … any drink with alcohol in it]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **vinegar** that is made from **wine** or **intoxicating drink**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [vinegar made from wine and vinegar made from intoxicating drink]

Here, **vinegar** is a kind of sour liquid made from fermented wine or other fermented drinks. If your readers would not be familiar with what vinegar is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [sour juice of … sour juice of]

4.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [All the days he is separate]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **vine** that is connected with **wine**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from the vine from which wine is produced]

Here, **vine** represents everything that comes from grape vines. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the grapes of the vine]

The expression **is made** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [from all that anyone makes]

Yahweh is referring to all parts of a grape by naming two major components, **seeds** and **skin**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from any part of a grape]

5.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **vow** that is characterized by **separation**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vow in which he swore separation]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his vow to be separate]

A **razor** is a kind of tool for cutting hair. If your readers would not be familiar with what a razor is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a shaving tool]

Yahweh is using **a razor shall not pass over upon his head** as a common expression of this culture to mean “he must not cut his hair.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a razor shall not be used on his head]
Here, **head** represents the hair on the head. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair on his head]

Yahweh is using the phrase **made separate to Yahweh** as a common expression of his culture to mean “set himself apart for Yahweh” or “dedicated himself to Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:2. Alternate translation: [that he set himself apart for Yahweh]
The implication is that **shall make great** means to let the hair grow long. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and shall grow out]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **locks** that are **the hair** that is on **his head**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the hairs on his head]

6.note: The phrase **making separate to Yahweh** is a common expression of this culture that means “dedicating oneself to Yahweh” or “setting oneself apart for Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:2. Alternate translation: [him setting himself apart for Yahweh]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of being close to a dead **person** as if one could literally **go upon** them. This refers to approaching a dead body. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he shall not come close to a person having died]

7.q: לְ⁠אָבִ֣י⁠ו וּ⁠לְ⁠אִמּ֗⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָחִי⁠ו֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠אַ֣חֹת֔⁠וֹ לֹא־יִטַּמָּ֥א לָ⁠הֶ֖ם בְּ⁠מֹתָ֑⁠ם כִּ֛י נֵ֥זֶר אֱלֹהָ֖י⁠ו עַל־רֹאשֽׁ⁠וֹ
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since **because the separation of his God is upon his head** gives the reason for the result that **For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, he shall not make himself unclean for them in their death** describes. Alternate translation: [Since the separation of his God is upon his head, he shall not make himself unclean for his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, in their death.]

7.q: לְ⁠אָבִ֣י⁠ו וּ⁠לְ⁠אִמּ֗⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָחִי⁠ו֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠אַ֣חֹת֔⁠וֹ לֹא־יִטַּמָּ֥א לָ⁠הֶ֖ם בְּ⁠מֹתָ֑⁠ם
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about making himself **unclean** before the list of relatives (**his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister**). Alternate translation: [He shall not make himself unclean for his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, in their death]

Here, Yahweh refers to a person’s closest relatives to refer to any close relatives. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For any close relatives, even his father, mother, brother, and sister]

The terms **brother** and **sister** include both older and younger siblings. Your language may have its own term or expression for this relationship. Alternate translation: [for any brother or sister]

By **he shall not make himself unclean for them**, Yahweh means he must not participate in funeral rituals or come near the dead bodies of even his closest relatives. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [he shall not make himself unclean for them by coming close to them]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **death**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when they die]

Here, **separation** represents the hair that a Nazirite grew to show his dedication to God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair that represents the separation of his God]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **separation** that is directed toward **his God**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the separation for his God’s sake]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how he separated himself for his God]

8.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [All the days while he separates himself]

9.note: It might seem that the expression **a dying one dies** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [a person dies]

Yahweh is using **dies upon him** as a common expression of his culture to mean “dies close to him.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [dies close to him]

Here Yahweh is using a construction in which two words come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [very suddenly]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **suddenness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [unexpectedly]

The word translated as **and** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and so he makes unclean]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **head** that shows or represents **his separation**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his head that represents his separation]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his head that represents how he made himself separate]
Here, **head** represents the hair on the head. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair on the head]

9.q: וְ⁠גִלַּ֤ח רֹאשׁ⁠וֹ֙ בְּ⁠י֣וֹם טָהֳרָת֔⁠וֹ בַּ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֖י יְגַלְּחֶֽ⁠נּוּ
9.note: It might seem that the expression **he shall shave it** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [then he shall shave his head on the day of his purification, which is the seventh day]

Here, **head** represents the hair on the head of the Nazirite. The long hair was a visible sign of the Nazirite’s dedication to God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair on his head]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that a person who becomes unclean from being near a dead body must wait seven days before being purified, according to the law in Numbers 19:11–22. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on the day of his purification. That is the seventh day after he was near a dead body according to the law concerning impurity from corpses, and on that day he shall shave it]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **purification**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [on the day when he is purified]
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **the seventh day**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [day seven]

10.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **the eighth day**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [And on day eight]

Here, **sons of a pigeon** refers to young pigeons. Yahweh is speaking as if they were actually children of the mother bird. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [pigeons that are young]

11.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he shall atone]

Yahweh is using **for him from what he sinned** as a common expression of this culture to mean “to restore him after he had sinned.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to restore him after he sinned]

The implication is that the person was defiled by touching or being near a dead person. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [concerning the dead person]

Here, **head** represents the Nazirite’s hair, which showed that he was dedicated to God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair that will grow on his head]

12.note: Yahweh is using the expression **make separate** as a common expression of this culture to mean “set himself apart” or “dedicate himself.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:2. Alternate translation: [And he shall set himself apart for Yahweh during the days of his separation]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the days he is separate]

The expression **a son of his year** is a common expression of his culture that means “one year old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a year old]

Here, the text speaks of the first days of separation as if they could **fall**, meaning they would not count toward the total time of separation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the first days must not be included in the time of separation]

The implication is that this is the first period during which the Nazirite had taken the vow before he was made unclean. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the days before he was made unclean]

The expression **his separation was made unclean** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the dead body made his separation unclean]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [he was made unclean while he was separate]

Here, **separation** represents the condition or state of being set apart as a Nazirite. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he, during his time of separation,]

13.note: By **this**, Yahweh means the instructions that follow about what should happen when a Nazirite’s period of dedication is complete. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [What follows is the law concerning the Nazirite]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **Nazirite**. He means Nazirites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Nazirites]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the day** on which **the days** that make up his time of **separation** are fulfilled. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [On the day when the time during which he is separate is fulfilled]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. See how you translated this phrase in 6:12. Alternate translation: [the days he is separate]

Here, the pronoun **him** refers to the Nazirite. The pronoun **he** could refer to: (1) any person who could accompany the Nazirite. Alternate translation: [a person shall bring the Nazirite] or [the Nazirite shall be brought] (2) the Nazirite, who brings himself. Alternate translation: [the Nazirite shall bring himself]

14.note: Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb (**present**) and its object (**offering**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and he shall give his offering]

Yahweh is using the common expression of his culture **a son of his year** to mean “one year old.” See how you translated this phrase in 6:12. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a year old]

The phrase **a daughter of her year** is a common expression of the culture that means “a year old.” See how you translated the similar phrase “a son of his year” earlier in the verse. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a year old]

15.q: וְ⁠סַ֣ל מַצּ֗וֹת סֹ֤לֶת חַלֹּת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּ⁠שֶּׁ֔מֶן וּ⁠רְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּ⁠שָּׁ֑מֶן וּ⁠מִנְחָתָ֖⁠ם וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶֽם
15.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **their grain offering and their drink offerings** immediately after the sacrifices mentioned in verse 14, since these offerings accompany those sacrifices. Alternate translation: [and their grain offering and their drink offerings; and a basket of unleavened bread, flour of loaves mixed with the oil and wafers of unleavened bread anointed with the oil]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **a basket** that is characterized by having **unleavened bread** in it. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and a basket full of unleavened bread]

A **basket** is a kind of container used to hold and carry things. If your readers would not be familiar with what a basket is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and a box]

15.q: מַצּ֗וֹת סֹ֤לֶת חַלֹּת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּ⁠שֶּׁ֔מֶן וּ⁠רְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּ⁠שָּׁ֑מֶן
15.note: The implication is that there were two distinct types of unleavened bread in the basket - **loaves mixed with oil** and **wafers anointed with oil**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [unleavened bread of two types, both flour of loaves mixed with the oil and wafers of unleavened bread anointed with the oil]

15.q: סֹ֤לֶת חַלֹּת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּ⁠שֶּׁ֔מֶן וּ⁠רְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּ⁠שָּׁ֑מֶן
15.note: The phrase **flour of loaves mixed with the oil** refers to thick loaves of bread in which **oil** was mixed before cooking. The phrase **wafers of unleavened bread anointed with the oil** refers to thin loaves of bread on which **oil** was spread after cooking. If your readers would not be familiar with these kinds of bread, you could use the names of similar things that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [thick loaves made from flour and oil and thin loaves spread with oil]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **loaves** that are characterized by **flour**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [loaves made of flour]

The expression **mixed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is whoever cooked the bread. Alternate translation: [that someone has mixed]

Yahweh is not referring to specific portions of **oil**. He means oil in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [with oil … with oil]

The expression **anointed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is whoever cooked the bread. Alternate translation: [that someone has anointed]

The pronoun **their** refers to the grain offerings and drink offerings that go with the sacrificial animals mentioned in verse 14. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the grain offering and drink offerings for each of those sacrifices]

In this verse, the word **grain offering** is singular in form, but it refers to all the grain offerings as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “grain offering.” Alternate translation: [and their grain offerings]

16.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply **the offerings** from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And the priest shall present the offerings]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

The pronoun **his** refers to the Nazirite, while the pronoun **he** refers to the priest. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the priest shall make the Nazirite’s sin offering and his burnt offering]

17.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **sacrifice** that is characterized by being part of the **peace offering**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the sacrifice that is part of the peace offering]

Yahweh is using **upon the basket** as a common expression of this culture to mean “along with the basket.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [along with the basket]

A **basket** is a kind of container made from woven material. If your readers would not be familiar with what a basket is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. See how you translated **basket** in 6:15. Alternate translation: [upon the box]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **basket** that is characterized by **the unleavened bread**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated this phrase in 6:15. Alternate translation: [the basket full of unleavened bread]

Here, the pronoun **his** could refer to: (1) the Nazirite who brought the **grain offering** and **drink offering**. Alternate translation: [the Nazirite’s grain offering and his drink offering] (2) the **peace offering**. Alternate translation: [its grain offering and its drink offering]

18.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:9. The only difference here is that the second phrase makes **hair** explicit. Alternate translation: [the hair on his head that represents how he made himself separate … the hair on his head that represents how he made himself separate]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that **the fire** was burning on the altar and that the peace offering was being sacrificed on that altar. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the fire that burns on the altar under]
See how you translated this phrase in 6:17.

19.note: This means that he had boiled the ram’s shoulder. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the shoulder of the ram that he boiled]

Here, the word **shoulder** refers to one of the front legs of the **ram**. The word **boiled** indicates that it has been cooked in hot water. If your readers would not be familiar with what a **boiled shoulder** is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [the front leg of the ram that has been cooked]

19.q: וְֽ⁠חַלַּ֨ת מַצָּ֤ה אַחַת֙ מִן־הַ⁠סַּ֔ל וּ⁠רְקִ֥יק מַצָּ֖ה אֶחָ֑ד
19.note: The phrase **one loaf of unleavened bread** refers to a thick loaf of bread in which oil was mixed before cooking. The phrase **one wafer of unleavened bread** refers to a thin loaf of bread on which **oil** was spread after cooking. See how you referred to these kinds of bread in 6:15. Alternate translation: [one thick unleavened loaf from the basket and one thin unleavened loaf]

A **basket** is a kind of container made from woven materials. If your readers would not be familiar with what a basket is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. See how you translated **basket** in 6:15. Alternate translation: [from the box]

Yahweh is using **on the palms of the Nazirite** as a common expression of this culture to mean “to give to the Nazirite to hold.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall give them to the Nazirite to hold]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how he made himself separate]

Here, **separation** represents the hair that showed that this person was separated to God as a Nazirite. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the hair that represents his separation]

20.note: The implication is that the Nazirite first gives these items to the priest, who then lifts them up as an offering. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the Nazirite shall hand them back to the priest, and the priest shall raise them]

The expression **raised offering** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [as an offering that the priests raise … the offering that the priests raise]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

The pronoun **It** refers to the portions of the sacrifice that the priest has raised up to Yahweh (the meat and bread). Yahweh is referring to those things as a group. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [They are holy things]

20.q: עַ֚ל חֲזֵ֣ה הַ⁠תְּנוּפָ֔ה וְ⁠עַ֖ל שׁ֣וֹק הַ⁠תְּרוּמָ֑ה
20.note: Yahweh assumes that readers will know that the breast and thigh portions of peace offerings were always given to the priests as their share of the offering. See Leviticus 7:28–34 for more information on this. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [upon the breast of the raised offering and upon the thigh of the contribution that are always given to the priest from any peace offering]

20.q: עַ֚ל חֲזֵ֣ה הַ⁠תְּנוּפָ֔ה וְ⁠עַ֖ל שׁ֣וֹק הַ⁠תְּרוּמָ֑ה
20.note: The phrase **upon the breast … and upon the thigh** is a common expression of this culture that means “in addition to the breast and thigh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [along with the breast of … and along with the thigh of]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **breast** that is offered as **the raised offering**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the breast that is presented as a raised offering]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **thigh** that is a **contribution**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the thigh that is contributed]

Yahweh is using a future statement to give an instruction or command in **the Nazirite will drink wine**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words using a command or instruction form. Alternate translation: [the Nazirite is allowed to drink wine]

21.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **Nazirite**. He means Nazirites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. See how you translated the similar phrase in 6:13. Alternate translation: [the Nazirites]

By **upon his separation**, Yahweh means after the time of being a Nazirite is completed. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who vows to present this offering to Yahweh after his separation]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [after he has been separate]

Yahweh is using **what his hand reaches** as a common expression of this culture to mean “whatever else he can give” or “whatever more he can afford.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [whatever else he can give]

Yahweh is speaking of **his vow** as if it were a living thing that had a **mouth**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [According to the words of his vow]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [what he vowed]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **separation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the law concerning when people make themselves separate]

23.q: אָמ֖וֹר לָ⁠הֶֽם & יְבָרֶכְ⁠ךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה וְ⁠יִשְׁמְרֶֽ⁠ךָ & יָאֵ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה ׀ פָּנָ֛י⁠ו אֵלֶ֖י⁠ךָ וִֽ⁠יחֻנֶּֽ⁠ךָּ & יִשָּׂ֨א יְהוָ֤ה ׀ פָּנָי⁠ו֙ אֵלֶ֔י⁠ךָ וְ⁠יָשֵׂ֥ם לְ⁠ךָ֖ שָׁלֽוֹם
23.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [telling them that they pray that Yahweh may bless them and keep them, that they pray that Yahweh may make his face shine to them and be gracious to them, and that they pray that Yahweh may lift up his face to them and put peace to them.]

23.q: דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְ⁠אֶל־בָּנָ֣י⁠ו לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה תְבָרֲכ֖וּ
23.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak to Aaron and to his sons. Tell them that this is how they shall bless]

24.q: יְבָרֶכְ⁠ךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה וְ⁠יִשְׁמְרֶֽ⁠ךָ & יָאֵ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה ׀ פָּנָ֛י⁠ו אֵלֶ֖י⁠ךָ וִֽ⁠יחֻנֶּֽ⁠ךָּ & יִשָּׂ֨א יְהוָ֤ה ׀ פָּנָי⁠ו֙ אֵלֶ֔י⁠ךָ וְ⁠יָשֵׂ֥ם לְ⁠ךָ֖ שָׁלֽוֹם
24.note: The priests are asking God to bless the Israelites. In your translation, use a form that people would recognize as a blessing in your language. You might express this as a prayer, if that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [We pray that Yahweh will bless you and keep you. We pray that Yahweh will make his face shine to you and be gracious to you. We pray that Yahweh will lift up his face to you and put peace to you.]

The word **you** is singular here because God is telling Aaron and his sons to bless each individual Israelite. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. Alternate translation: [May Yahweh bless each one of you, and may he keep each one of you]

25.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if his **face** were actually shining on someone with light. This refers to him acting favorably toward them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [May Yahweh favor you]

The word **you** is singular here because this blessing was originally spoken to each individual Israelite. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. Alternate translation: [to each of you, and may he be gracious to each of you]

26.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if Yahweh had a physical **face** that he could lift up toward someone. This expression means that Yahweh would pay attention to someone in order to help them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [May Yahweh pay attention to you for your good]

The word **you** is singular here because Aaron and his sons are speaking this blessing to each individual Israelite. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. Alternate translation: [to each of you … to each of you]

Yahweh is using **put peace to you** as a common expression of this culture to mean “give you peace” or “cause you to have peace.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he give you peace]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and may he make you live peacefully]

27.note: Here, God is speaking of Aaron and his sons **putting his name** on the Israelites as if his name were a physical object that could be placed on them. This means that the priests will declare that the Israelites belong to God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they shall call the sons of Israel mine] or [And they shall link the sons of Israel with me through the use of my name]

The word **and** here indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and as a result I, I will bless them]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I will bless** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who will do the blessing. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that emphasis. Alternate translation: [and it is I who will bless them]
